findings.summary: On original labels, Thornbill-NER achieves a mean test F1 of 91.4% ± 0.4%, with a worst-seed F1 of 90.9% and a seed range of 0.9 points; Lindgren-Tagger achieves 90.8% ± 0.5%, worst-seed 90.1%, range 1.2 points.
findings.scope: Corvane-News NER test set, original training labels, 5 seeds (0–4), entity-level F1
findings.caveats: No statistical tests reported; differences in means and ranges are descriptive only.

findings.summary: The research question about robustness to label noise cannot be answered from the supplied evidence, because no experiments with perturbed or noisy training labels are reported.
findings.caveats: The package only contains results for original-label training; no noise conditions or robustness comparisons are provided.

drafts.passage: On the original Corvane-News NER labels, Thornbill-NER achieved a mean test F1 of 91.4% ± 0.4% with a worst-seed F1 of 90.9% and a seed range of 0.9 points, while Lindgren-Tagger achieved 90.8% ± 0.5% with a worst-seed F1 of 90.1% and a seed range of 1.2 points.
